intervention_label: Active surveillance — structured cross-sectional imaging q3-6 months for 2-3 years then space out; PGL/PCC surveillance (plasma free metanephrines + whole-body MRI baseline); no adjuvant systemic therapy
expected_benefit: Preserves every downstream option at zero therapeutic toxicity. The natural history (Mei 2018, NIH 76-patient surgical cohort: median EFS ~2.5 yr post-resection, ~71% eventual recurrence) argues for imaging surveillance over a regimen the molecular evidence rejects. Boikos 2016 anchors the empirical no on adjuvant imatinib: 1/49 (2%) PR in dSDH-GIST.
key_risks: Recurrence is the expectation (~71%), so the imaging schedule has to actually run on time or the indolence argument stops protecting the patient
Scan-anxiety burden of indefinite follow-up is a real soft cost, not captured in any toxicity table and not yet elicited
Multifocal primary plus a resected M1 deposit puts this patient past the cleanest localized-primary natural-history cohorts, so the 2.5-yr mEFS is a floor not a ceiling
An undetected functional paraganglioma in an SDHx carrier going to anesthesia is a hypertensive-crisis hazard, which is why the PGL baseline pairs with the imaging plan
preference_alignment: matches efficacy/toxicity weight 0.65: YES (no chronic toxicity committed for a low-yield mechanism in NED disease); matches prefers_trials: PARTIAL (registry at rank 3 carries the trial axis; surveillance itself is not a trial)
guideline_status: NCCN GIST v1.2026 and ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS 2022 both recommend AGAINST adjuvant imatinib in SDH-deficient GIST; surveillance is the cross-society default.
rationale_summary: Every persona lands here as the now-move. Four ranked it first outright (advocate, concensusite, conservative, critic) and the risktaker, who led with a systemic agent, says plainly in their notes that an NED patient gets no adjuvant therapy, which is the same call. The concensusite framed the cross-society convergence cleanly: NCCN and ESMO both put SDH-expression-negative GIST in the avoid-adjuvant column because the subset does not respond to imatinib and runs indolent. The advocate added the option-preservation argument, that starting a TKI now would burn screening eligibility for the contingency trials this patient prefers. The conservative anchored the toxicity side: even if the adjuvant-imatinib RCTs transported, which they do not since dSDH-GIST was never enrolled, three years of edema and fatigue against a 2% return fails the tolerability weight under any reading. The risktaker's one push, that surveillance should be active rather than passive (chase FGFR access, finish the SDHB re-cut now), is a sharpening of this row, not a dissent against it.
open_questions: Geography and travel tolerance, unspecified, gate registry enrollment and which recurrence trials are reachable
Scan-anxiety tolerance, the real cost of indefinite imaging-based follow-up, has not been elicited
Whole-body MRI versus CT as the surveillance backbone (cumulative-radiation versus payer-auth tradeoff)
likelihood_of_effect: Effect is option-preservation, not tumor control. Cross-society guidelines plus Boikos 2016 (imatinib 1/49 PR) close adjuvant systemic therapy in this subset.
toxicity_burden: Low (none — imaging surveillance and biochemical screening have no AE profile; the soft cost is scan anxiety)

counter_productive_moa.description: Non-therapeutic management pathway — no mechanism-level risk to a therapeutic goal.

overall: Guideline-aligned lead for NED dSDH-GIST; no adjuvant agent bends the recurrence curve, so committing chronic toxicity now buys nothing and forecloses option space.

intervention_label: SDHB + SDHA IHC re-cut with positive internal control + germline SDHA panel + tumor-tissue NGS confirmation of the ctDNA-only variants (one-tissue-pull diagnostic gate)
expected_benefit: Resolves three load-bearing questions in one tissue pull: (1) is SDHA L306P germline (cascade testing + lifetime PGL surveillance) or somatic (biallelic somatic loss); (2) does SDHA IHC loss reconcile the SDHB-intact / SDHA-biallelic paradox so the dSDH-GIST label survives a trial screener; (3) are PIK3CA R93W, MAP2K1 P124S, and SDHA E350fs clonal in tumor or ctDNA-only artifacts. Decisive for enrollment on every dSDH-GIST trial, which uses SDHB-IHC loss as the entry phenotype.
key_risks: No therapeutic toxicity — germline blood draw, IHC re-cut on archival FFPE, comprehensive tumor NGS
Adds 2-4 weeks of turnaround before any recurrence contingency can move

If SDHB AND SDHA IHC both read intact after a clean re-stain, the dSDH label collapses and the trial-route options foreclose; the case becomes a molecularly-deficient / immunohistochemically-proficient outlier and SDHC promoter methylation becomes the next fallback call
preference_alignment: matches prefers_trials: YES (every dSDH-GIST trial gates on SDHB-IHC loss plus a confirmed driver); matches efficacy/toxicity weight 0.65: neutral (diagnostic, no therapeutic effect)
guideline_status: Standard SDHx workup per the 2025 Florou review (pmid:39927693); NCCN GIST v1.2026 directs genetic-counseling and germline referral for every SDH-deficient GIST; SDHA IHC orthogonal arbitration per Miettinen 2013 (pmid:23023976).
rationale_summary: All five personas demand this, whether they ranked it as a discrete pick (critic at 2, advocate at 3) or flagged it in their primary concerns (conservative: the re-cut needs to happen now; concensusite: the re-cut has to confirm the phenotype before the ESMO consensus attaches; risktaker: finish the SDHB re-cut so eligibility does not lag the recurrence). The biallelic SDHA call sits at ~85% combined VAF and should destabilize the complex and abolish SDHB staining, yet the report reads SDHB intact, and that discordance is the single most load-bearing flag in the case. The critic put it most sharply: every dSDH-GIST trial entry phenotype runs through SDHB-IHC loss, so this is a structural threat to the whole trial portfolio, not a footnote. The germline SDHA result drives cascade testing and the lifetime PGL program; the SDHA IHC arbitrates whether this is SDHA-driven (locked in regardless of the SDHB stain) or a non-SDHA SDHx driver where SDHC methylation is the fallback. There was no dissent and no veto.
open_questions: If SDHB stays intact after a clean re-stain and SDHA IHC is also retained, the next call is SDHC promoter methylation (academic referral, 4-8 weeks)
Whether PIK3CA R93W and MAP2K1 P124S confirm in tissue — if not, the PI3Kalpha and MEK pathways drop out entirely
Germline SDHA cascade-testing conversation should wait for the panel result (2-3 weeks)
likelihood_of_effect: Diagnostic certainty — resolves the SDHB paradox, confirms the dSDH driver, and gates trial eligibility (Florou 2025, pmid:39927693).
toxicity_burden: Low (none — diagnostic: germline blood draw, IHC re-cut on archival FFPE, comprehensive tumor NGS)

counter_productive_moa.description: Diagnostic, not therapeutic — no mechanism-level risk to a therapeutic goal.

overall: Resolves the SDHB-intact / biallelic-SDHA paradox in one tissue pull and locks the dSDH label every recurrence trial screens on.

intervention_label: NCI Rare Tumor Natural History Study enrollment (NCT03739827) + cancer-genetics counseling covering the SDHA germline result and POLE R1679C reclassification
expected_benefit: Zero-toxicity, highest yield-per-cost move in the dossier. Enrollment is open regardless of disease status, so the NED-post-R0 setting is not a blocker; it gives longitudinal follow-up at the NIH Pediatric and wt-GIST clinic, opens the SDHC promoter-methylation fallback assay if the SDHA workup collapses, and banks biospecimen that pays forward if a trial slot opens at recurrence. Pairs with genetics counseling once the germline SDHA panel returns; POLE R1679C lands on the VUS side of the ledger (outside the proofreading hotspots, TMB <1, MSS), so counseling closes that loop rather than triggering polyposis surveillance.
key_risks: Requires one in-person NIH baseline visit — travel is the operational cost and the patient's geography is unknown
Germline SDHA returns in 2-3 weeks; the cascade-testing conversation with relatives should wait for it
POLE counseling will most likely land on VUS — say so upfront so the result is not over-read
preference_alignment: matches prefers_trials: YES (the only trial enrollable today — no measurable-disease requirement, no investigational drug); matches efficacy/toxicity weight 0.65: YES (zero toxicity, infrastructure for every downstream option)
guideline_status: NCCN GIST v1.2026 directs genetic-counseling referral for all SDH-deficient GIST; Endocrine Society 2014 PPGL guidance points at the NIH wt-GIST clinic as the reference center, and registry enrollment is the entry door.
rationale_summary: Advocate and concensusite ranked this at 2, conservative bundled it into rank 1, and the risktaker named it explicitly in their plan; the critic neither ranked nor objected. Three structural arguments converge: the patient is NED so most contingency trials are blocked by measurable-disease requirements, but the registry is not; the SDHC-methylation fallback is essentially unavailable outside academic channels and the NIH clinic is the most accessible US path; and biospecimen banking now pays forward if PEMIGIST or LITESPARK-015 opens a slot at recurrence. The counseling visit folds the germline SDHA result and the POLE R1679C VUS framing into one coherent family-risk conversation rather than two staggered ones. No dissent, no veto; the only open variable is whether the patient's geography supports the baseline visit.
open_questions: Whether the patient's geography supports the NIH baseline visit, or whether OHSU / Texas Children's is the better operational fit
Whether the germline SDHA panel returns in time to inform the in-person visit or whether the visit runs first
Counselor's preferred sequencing — germline panel first, or counseling visit first
likelihood_of_effect: High infrastructure yield — NIH wt-GIST clinic access, SDHC-methylation fallback, biospecimen banking, and family cascade testing; no tumor-control claim.
toxicity_burden: Low (none — observational registry enrollment plus a counseling visit; one in-person NIH baseline)

counter_productive_moa.description: Infrastructure and counseling, not therapy — no mechanism-level risk to a therapeutic goal.

overall: Zero-toxicity trial enrollment open while NED, plus the genetics counseling NCCN requires for every SDH-deficient GIST.

intervention_label: Sunitinib 50 mg PO 4-on/2-off (or 37.5 mg continuous) at first measurable recurrence — NOT adjuvant
expected_benefit: Objective response 7/38 (18%) in the SDH-deficient subset versus 1/49 (2%) on imatinib (Boikos 2016) — the best-replicated systemic signal in this subtype. The agent's own pivotal is registration-grade (Demetri 2006, n=312, TTP HR 0.33, p<0.0001) though that population was overwhelmingly KIT-mutant with no SDH stratification.
key_risks: Fatigue, diarrhea, hand-foot skin reaction, skin discoloration, hypertension — well-worn management algorithms after two decades of post-marketing use
Baseline BP and skin monitoring needed from cycle 1
18% ORR is honest but unimpressive; a bulky or fast-moving recurrence may justify a less-charted agent
preference_alignment: matches efficacy/toxicity weight 0.65: PARTIAL (oral, predictable tox, modest ORR); prefers_trials: NO (FDA-approved, not a trial) — the advocate frames it as co-equal with the trial menu rather than the default first reach
guideline_status: NCCN GIST v1.2026 second-line option; ESMO 2022 prefers sunitinib over imatinib in dSDH-GIST on the Boikos 18%-vs-2% figures.
rationale_summary: This is the one FDA-approved, guideline-preferred contingency, and four personas placed it (concensusite, conservative, critic ranked it; advocate names it as the co-equal fallback). The concensusite calls it the consensus opening move at recurrence; the conservative ranks it first among systemic agents precisely because its toxicity tail is the most predictable on the table. The critic agrees but reads the 18% as directional rather than dependable, since Boikos is retrospective (ROBINS-I Moderate) with small per-drug n and the Demetri HR comes from a KIT-mutant population that does not transport cleanly. The advocate's one push, registered as a preference qualification not a dissent, is that for a trial-preferring patient the trial menu should sit alongside sunitinib rather than behind it. There was no dissent against sunitinib itself and no veto. It is conditional on the dSDH confirmation only in the sense that the whole recurrence plan is; sunitinib would be reached at measurable recurrence regardless of the exact WT-GIST subtype.
open_questions: Whether a future recurrence is indolent enough to favor sunitinib's predictability or bulky enough to justify a higher-ORR but less-charted agent
Per-AE G3+ rates in a dSDH-specific population are not separately characterized (Boikos has no per-AE table)
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate-to-low in dSDH-GIST: 7/38 (18%) objective response, Boikos 2016 — the best-replicated systemic signal, but well below KIT-mutant activity.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (fatigue, hand-foot skin reaction, hypertension, diarrhea)

counter_productive_moa.description: Anti-angiogenic VEGFR blockade can impair wound healing — relevant if a future re-resection is on the table.

overall: The one FDA-approved, guideline-preferred contingency with dSDH-specific data (18% ORR); modest but predictable where the newer agents are not.
scenario_label: If SDH-deficiency is confirmed on SDHB/SDHA IHC re-cut (loss) with germline SDHA resolution

intervention_label: Temozolomide (MGMT-methylation-enriched), trial route preferred (NCT05661643 / NCT03556384) at first measurable recurrence
expected_benefit: 2/5 (40%) PR with 100% disease control in SDH-mutant GIST (Yebra 2022), with the benefit biomarker-selectable: MGMT promoter hypermethylation occurs in 8/33 (24%) of dSDH-GIST and 0% elsewhere (Giger 2022), so methylation testing enriches for likely responders before exposing anyone to an alkylator.
key_risks: Myelosuppression (thrombocytopenia, neutropenia), fatigue, nausea — predictable but real, and not worth incurring in an MGMT-unmethylated tumor
n=5 is the entire prospective efficacy base in this subtype, so the 40% ORR is fragile
Enrolling trial NCT05661643 is Korea-based (Asan) and requires measurable disease
preference_alignment: matches prefers_trials: YES (NCT05661643 recruiting); matches efficacy/toxicity weight 0.65: PARTIAL (oral, MGMT-gated benefit, cytopenia cost); no toxicity vetoes on file
guideline_status: Off-guideline as a standard agent; NCCN GIST v1.2026 endorses clinical-trial enrollment for SDH-deficient GIST, so the guideline fit is the trial route, not the drug.
rationale_summary: Four personas placed temozolomide (concensusite ranked the trial route at 5, conservative at 3, risktaker at 4, critic at 6 as a late contingency). The status is considered_with_caveats despite no formal dissent because the option is doubly gated: it needs both the dSDH confirmation AND MGMT methylation (~24% prevalence, status unknown here), and the entire clinical signal rests on a 5-patient series. The conservative would gate any commitment on MGMT testing first to avoid pushing an unselected patient through cytopenias; the critic frames it the same way, as a contingency he would run only on a trial with MGMT enrichment, calling the n=5 hypothesis-generating rather than supportive of a default off-label move. The concensusite is explicit that what is guideline-aligned here is the trial-enrollment route, not temozolomide as a standard agent. Order the MGMT test now so the result is ready if recurrence makes this live.
open_questions: The patient's MGMT methylation status is unknown; only ~24% of dSDH-GIST are methylated
Whether travel to Asan (NCT05661643) is feasible, or whether NCT03556384 (UCSD, active-not-recruiting) reopens
Whether the Yebra 40% ORR holds beyond n=5 once a trial reads out
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate only if MGMT-methylated (~24% of dSDH-GIST): 2/5 PR, Yebra 2022; low or absent in unmethylated tumors. Gate on testing.

counter_productive_moa.description: Alkylator exposure without MGMT methylation incurs cytopenias for little antitumor effect; theoretical hypermutation/resistance risk over long use.

overall: Highest reported ORR (40%, n=5) but only in the ~24% MGMT-methylated subset; gate on methylation testing before exposing anyone to alkylator cytopenias.
scenario_label: If SDH-deficiency is confirmed on SDHB/SDHA IHC re-cut (loss) with germline SDHA resolution

intervention_label: Olverembatinib (HQP1351, multikinase inhibitor), trial route only (phase 1b signal; phase-3 NCT06640361) at first measurable recurrence
expected_benefit: 6/26 (23.1%, 95% CI 9-43.7) confirmed PR with mPFS 25.7 mo (95% CI 12.9-NR) in the dSDH-GIST cohort (Qiu 2025) — the largest prospective trial to date in the subtype, with the cleanest safety sheet in the dossier (grade >=3 TRAE 13.6%, zero AE-related discontinuations across the 66-patient phase 1b).
key_risks: Anemia (G3+ 6.1%), transaminase rise, hyperuricemia, leukocytosis — familiar and monitorable; safety figures are pooled across the full 66-patient basket, not the 26-patient GIST cohort
Phase 1b n=26; the 25.7-mo PFS could shrink in a randomized setting
The phase-3 NCT06640361 entry criterion is SDHB-IHC loss, which this patient's stain does not currently show until the re-cut resolves it
preference_alignment: matches prefers_trials: YES (NCT06640361) but China-sited (Ascentage), so access is a separate problem from eligibility; matches efficacy/toxicity weight 0.65: PARTIAL (oral, cleanest safety, ORR roughly half the rogaratinib signal)
guideline_status: Not in NCCN or ESMO; trial-territory (phase 1b plus the registrational-in-name NCT06640361).
rationale_summary: Three personas placed it (risktaker at 3, conservative at 4, critic at 5), and the advocate named it in the recurrence trial menu. The status is considered_with_caveats on two structural grounds the board agreed on rather than on a dissent. First, the critic pushed the design caveat past the conservative's: NCT06640361, labeled phase 3, is single-arm with a PFS-rate endpoint and no comparator, so even at completion it will not deliver randomized evidence. Second, the mechanism is non-canonical for a KIT/PDGFRA-WT tumor — this is a KIT/ABL TKI acting through VEGFR/FGFR/HIF-CD36 axes, so plausibility is borrowed, not demonstrated in-indication. The risktaker values it most for the tolerability, which matters for a patient in their 40s who may be on therapy for years. The SDHB-IHC-loss entry mismatch is the live access risk: if the re-cut shows SDHA-IHC loss but SDHB stays intact, this trial may still screen-fail.
open_questions: Whether subtype-specific tolerability holds once safety is reported for the n=26 GIST cohort rather than the pooled 66
Whether Ascentage access outside China is workable
Whether the SDHB-IHC-loss entry criterion can be met or waived given the patient's intact stain
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate: 6/26 (23.1%) PR, mPFS 25.7 mo (Qiu 2025) in the exact subtype, but a single phase-1b cohort, unreplicated.
toxicity_burden: Low (anemia, transaminitis, hyperuricemia, leukocytosis — all G3+ rates < 20%)

counter_productive_moa.description: Non-canonical MoA in a KIT-WT tumor; efficacy borrows from VEGFR/FGFR/HIF-CD36 axes, not the labeled KIT/ABL target.

overall: Cleanest safety sheet and replicated dSDH activity (23.1% ORR, 25.7-mo PFS), but phase 1b, China-sponsored, and its phase-3 entry needs SDHB-IHC loss this patient may not show.
scenario_label: If SDH-deficiency is confirmed on SDHB/SDHA IHC re-cut (loss) with germline SDHA resolution

intervention_label: Rogaratinib (pan-FGFR1-4 inhibitor), trial route only (NCI cohort closed to accrual; FGFR-pathway evidence anchor) at first measurable recurrence
expected_benefit: 10/24 (41.7%) PR with mPFS 31.0 mo (95% CI 20.2-NR) and 1-year PFS 77.4% (Merriam 2026) — the highest objective response rate yet reported for any systemic agent in dSDH-GIST, in the exact molecular population, with a preclinically grounded FGF4-insulator mechanism (Flavahan 2019).
key_risks: Hyperphosphatemia (the pan-FGFR class effect, tracked target engagement), fatigue, diarrhea — but per-grade rates are not retrievable from the abstract, the empty CT.gov results tab, or the paywalled full text, so the toxicity is unverified
Single-arm open-label n=24, no comparator; the 91.7% DCR may be inflated by dSDH indolence, though the 41.7% PR fraction stands as tumor regression
Closed to accrual and Bayer has stepped back from the program, so access likely means compassionate use, not enrollment
preference_alignment: prefers_trials: trial CLOSED (access via compassionate use only); efficacy/toxicity weight 0.65 (efficacy-leaning) favors the 41.7% ORR, but the unverified AE table undercuts the toxicity side of that weight
guideline_status: Not in NCCN or ESMO; a pre-guideline single-arm signal.
rationale_summary: This is the most contested row on the board. The risktaker ranked it first as the biggest swing on the table; the critic and conservative placed it but low (4 and 5) and dissented in round 2 against the first-place call. The concensusite is the clean dissent: a single-arm n=24 cohort closed to accrual appears in no guideline, so it cannot head the plan. The conservative's objection is a safety one — ranking first the one agent whose per-grade AE distribution cannot be retrieved is the trade he pushes back on — and he is explicit it is a dissent on toxicity, not a veto, since no measurable disease is being treated today. The critic's is an evidence one — an n=24 response signal is not confirmatory, and the confirmatory pemigatinib cohort has not read out. The risktaker's counter, which I find partly persuasive, is that the indolence-inflates-DCR argument lands on the 50% SD fraction, not on the 10/24 confirmed PR. Net: a real, possibly best-in-subtype efficacy signal held to trial-route-only by an access wall and an unverifiable safety table.
open_questions: Whether a compassionate-use path to rogaratinib exists now that Bayer has stepped back and the NCI cohort is closed
Whether the per-grade AE table ever becomes retrievable from the full Nature Medicine paper
Whether the pemigatinib cohort (NCT07434843) replicates the FGFR-pathway signal
likelihood_of_effect: Highest reported: 10/24 (41.7%) PR, mPFS 31 mo (Merriam 2026), but single-arm n=24 and unreplicated; DCR may overstate via indolence.
toxicity_burden: Unresolved (per-grade AE table not retrievable; class hyperphosphatemia, fatigue, diarrhea reported without grades)

counter_productive_moa.description: Single-arm DCR may reflect dSDH indolence rather than drug effect; the FGFR-pathway dependence is unreplicated.

overall: Best ORR yet in dSDH-GIST (41.7%), but single-arm n=24, AE table unretrievable, and the trial is closed to accrual — access, not efficacy, is the wall.
scenario_label: If SDH-deficiency is confirmed on SDHB/SDHA IHC re-cut (loss) with germline SDHA resolution

intervention_label: Belzutifan (HIF-2alpha inhibitor) 120 mg PO daily, off-label or LITESPARK-015 wt-GIST cohort (NCT04924075) at first measurable recurrence
expected_benefit: The most direct shot at the actual driver: SDH loss drives succinate accumulation and HIF-2alpha stabilization (Selak 2005; Bayley 2022 SDHB model), the node belzutifan blocks. The sibling SDH-loss disease provides the only efficacy anchor — the PPGL cohort of LITESPARK-015 showed ORR 26% with mPFS 22 mo. No dSDH-GIST readout exists yet.
key_risks: Anemia and fatigue are expected HIF-2alpha class effects; the anemia is compounded here by the patient's Roux-en-Y anatomy (B12/iron malabsorption)
Hypoxia is a labelled risk
No published dSDH-GIST efficacy — the case rests on mechanism plus the PPGL cross-indication cohort
preference_alignment: matches efficacy/toxicity weight 0.65: PARTIAL (oral, accessible off-label so access does not hinge on enrollment); prefers_trials: PARTIAL (the wt-GIST cohort of NCT04924075 is recruiting but pre-readout)
guideline_status: Not in NCCN or ESMO for GIST; approved off-label (RCC / VHL-associated tumors, PPGL); the wt-GIST cohort is trial-territory.
rationale_summary: Two personas placed it (risktaker at 5, advocate in the recurrence trial menu, where the advocate called it the cleanest mechanism case with US sites open). The status is considered_with_caveats because the evidence is mechanism plus cross-indication only, with no GIST readout. The risktaker is candid about the limit and supplies the cautionary precedent himself: guadecitabine, another mechanistically matched agent for the same hypermethylation biology, returned 0/9 in this subtype, a reminder that target validation does not guarantee a clinical response. What belzutifan has that the FGFR agents lack is access — it is approved off-label, so a recurrence does not have to wait for a trial slot. The HIF-2alpha pipeline beyond it has thinned (DFF332 and NKT-2152 both discontinued), leaving belzutifan as the sole active HIF-2alpha option.
open_questions: When the wt-GIST cohort of LITESPARK-015 (NCT04924075) reads out (watch ASCO 2026 / WCGIC)
Whether the Roux-en-Y anatomy worsens the HIF-2alpha-class anemia beyond the usual management
Whether cross-indication PPGL activity transports to dSDH-GIST
likelihood_of_effect: Uncertain in GIST — no readout; cross-indication PPGL cohort ORR 26% (LITESPARK-015) in sibling SDH-loss biology is the only efficacy anchor.

counter_productive_moa.description: Direct driver-axis blockade, but a mechanism-matched agent (guadecitabine) failed in this subtype — target engagement may not translate.

overall: Most direct shot at the HIF-2alpha driver and accessible off-label, but no GIST readout and a mechanism-matched precedent (guadecitabine) already failed.
scenario_label: If SDH-deficiency is confirmed on SDHB/SDHA IHC re-cut (loss) with germline SDHA resolution

intervention_label: Pemigatinib (FGFR1-3 inhibitor), PEMIGIST trial route (NCT07434843, recruiting, DFCI) at first measurable recurrence
expected_benefit: Same FGFR pathway as rogaratinib but through a door that is actually open — NCT07434843 (George/DFCI) recruits in this exact subtype. The pathway logic carries across the two agents: the SDH-deficient PDX work responded to pemigatinib, not only rogaratinib (Flavahan 2019; shared preclinical models), and the rogaratinib readout (41.7% ORR) is the clinical signal it rides on.
key_risks: FGFR class effects — hyperphosphatemia, stomatitis, nail/skin changes, serous retinal detachment — on a days-1-14-of-21 schedule that needs phosphate and ophthalmologic monitoring
No clinical efficacy data in dSDH-GIST yet; the bet rides on the rogaratinib readout plus the shared PDX response
Requires measurable disease, so it is a recurrence option, not a now-move
preference_alignment: matches prefers_trials: YES (recruiting, DFCI — the open FGFR door the advocate flagged); matches efficacy/toxicity weight 0.65: PARTIAL (oral, no efficacy data of its own yet)
guideline_status: Not in NCCN or ESMO; a recruiting in-subtype phase-2 (24-patient single-arm).
rationale_summary: The risktaker ranked it second, explicitly as how to cash the FGFR bet if rogaratinib stays unreachable, and the advocate named it as the open-trial route for the FGFR signal — lead with the door that opens. The status is considered_with_caveats because there is no clinical readout: the entire rationale rests on the rogaratinib signal and the shared PDX response, and it is another 24-patient single-arm design. For a trial-preferring patient this is the more actionable of the two FGFR options precisely because it is recruiting and US-based, even though rogaratinib carries the higher published number. Suzanne George at DFCI is the logical referral path.
open_questions: When NCT07434843 produces a first readout
Whether pemigatinib reproduces the rogaratinib FGFR signal or whether the pathway dependence proves agent-specific
Whether measurable disease will be present at the time a slot is open
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown — no clinical readout in dSDH-GIST; the rationale rests on the rogaratinib FGFR signal and a shared PDX response (pmid:31666694).
toxicity_burden: Moderate (hyperphosphatemia, stomatitis, serous retinal detachment, nail/skin changes)

counter_productive_moa.description: FGFR-pathway bet with no clinical readout; shares rogaratinib's unreplicated-pathway uncertainty.

overall: The open FGFR door — recruiting in-subtype — but riding entirely on the rogaratinib signal and shared preclinical models, with no clinical readout of its own.
scenario_label: If SDH-deficiency is confirmed on SDHB/SDHA IHC re-cut (loss) with germline SDHA resolution

intervention_label: Regorafenib 160 mg PO 3-weeks-on/1-off, guideline-sequenced 3L TKI after sunitinib at recurrence
expected_benefit: GRID pivotal: PFS HR 0.27 (95% CI 0.19-0.39, p<0.0001), mPFS 4.8 vs 0.9 mo (Demetri 2013) — but in a KIT-mutant-dominated population. The dSDH-specific claim is qualitative: modest activity, similar to the KIT-mutant 3L setting (von Mehren 2025 review).
key_risks: Hand-foot skin reaction (G3+ 20%), hypertension (G3+ 23%), diarrhea (G3+ 5%) — characteristic VEGFR-TKI class burden
No dSDH-GIST-specific trial data; the subset claim rests on extrapolation from a KIT-mutant pivotal
Contingency only, and only after sunitinib in the guideline sequence
preference_alignment: matches efficacy/toxicity weight 0.65: PARTIAL (oral, but a real hand-foot / hypertension burden); prefers_trials: NO (FDA-approved 3L, not a trial)
guideline_status: NCCN GIST v1.2026 and ESMO 2022 sequence regorafenib third-line after sunitinib, on GRID.
rationale_summary: Only the concensusite ranked it (at 4), as the guideline-aligned third-line rung of the contingency ladder, and the critic qualified that placement rather than dissenting — GRID is RoB2 Low for the agent, but the population was KIT-mutant and dSDH-GIST under-represented, so the rung rests on extrapolation, not subtype data, and the NCCN sequencing is category 2A consensus rather than RCT-level proof in this genotype. Status is considered_with_caveats on that evidence gap. It earns a place as the established 3L option once sunitinib is exhausted, with the inference gap stated out loud rather than letting the HR 0.27 carry weight it did not earn in this subtype.
open_questions: Whether dSDH-GIST activity matches the qualitative modest claim or falls below it

intervention_label: Adjuvant imatinib — NOT RECOMMENDED in dSDH-GIST (logged so the reflex GIST-means-imatinib call is documented, not re-litigated)
expected_benefit: None to speak of: 1/49 (2%) PR in dSDH-GIST on imatinib (Boikos 2016). The registration adjuvant RCTs (Z9001, SSGXVIII, PERSIST-5) enrolled KIT-driven disease and structurally excluded this subtype, so their benefit does not transport.
key_risks: Three years of periorbital edema, fatigue, cytopenias, rash, and hepatic/cardiac monitoring burden for a 2% return
Spends the screening eligibility for the contingency trials the patient prefers
preference_alignment: efficacy/toxicity weight 0.65: FAILS outright (three years of toxicity for ~2% response); prefers_trials: FAILS (not a trial, and it burns trial-screening eligibility)
guideline_status: ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS 2022 recommends AGAINST adjuvant imatinib in SDH-deficient GIST; NCCN GIST v1.2026 concurs.
rationale_summary: Logged as a veto by the advocate, on the patient's behalf, so the reflex GIST-means-imatinib reach is documented and not re-litigated on the post-op note. It is kept in the table as not_recommended rather than dropped, per the no-silent-veto rule, so the reader sees what was considered and rejected. The concensusite, conservative, and critic all reach the same conclusion independently: the subset was never represented in the adjuvant RCTs and does not respond, so withholding it is the guideline call, not a judgment call. There is no version of the efficacy-toxicity weight that rescues a 2% response against three years of chronic toxicity. I am not overriding the veto.
open_questions: None — the no-adjuvant-imatinib call is firm given the confirmed KIT/PDGFRA-WT genotype
likelihood_of_effect: Effectively none — 1/49 (2%) PR in dSDH-GIST (Boikos 2016); the molecular subset does not respond.

counter_productive_moa.description: Targets KIT, which is wild-type here; near-inactive in dSDH-GIST (2% response) while committing years of toxicity.

overall: Reflex GIST-means-imatinib reach, documented as rejected: KIT is wild-type, response is ~2%, and three years of toxicity buys nothing here.
